---
title: "Prepare baby names by decade"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    toc: true
    df-print: paged
execute:
  echo: true
  message: false
---

Which names were popular in each generation? We use U.S. birth counts for the 14 complete decades from 1880–2019.

## Packages and helpers
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
source("R/helpers.R")
```

## Read the annual files
Each annual file has a name, sex and birth count. Build the filenames for 1880–2019, then combine those files with `read_csv()`. Keep the source filename so we can identify each row’s year.
```{r}
#| label: read-baby-names
ssa_years <- 1880:2019
ssa_file_paths <- str_c("data/raw/ssa/yob", ssa_years, ".txt")
ssa_raw <- read_csv(
  ssa_file_paths,
  col_names = c("original_name", "sex", "births"),
  col_types = cols(original_name = col_character(), sex = col_character(), births = col_integer()),
  id = "source_file", na = character()
)
```

## Give names the same matching format as the dogs
Extract the year from the filename. For example, `yob1924.txt` supplies 1924. Integer division by ten groups years into decades, so 1924 belongs to 1920.
```{r}
#| label: format-baby-names
ssa_raw |>
  mutate(
    source_filename = basename(source_file),
    name = str_to_upper(original_name, locale = "en")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = str_extract(source_filename, "[0-9]{4}"),
    name = str_remove_all(name, "[\\s-]")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(year),
    decade = (year %/% 10) * 10
  ) |>
  select(name, sex, year, decade, births) ->
  ssa_yearly
```

## Count names in each decade
Add births across all years and both sex categories. This measures how many babies received each name during the period.
```{r}
#| label: count-baby-names
ssa_yearly |>
  group_by(name, decade) |>
  summarise(births = sum(births), .groups = "drop") ->
  ssa_decade_counts
```

## Rank names within each decade
Order names by birth count, breaking ties alphabetically. Each decade gets exactly 100 top names. A name’s share divides its birth count by the decade’s total published births.
```{r}
#| label: rank-baby-names
ssa_decade_counts |>
  group_by(decade) |>
  arrange(desc(births), name, .by_group = TRUE, .locale = "C") |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(), share = births / sum(births), top100 = rank <= 100) |>
  ungroup() ->
  ssa_decades

ssa_decades |>
  filter(rank <= 5)
```

## Make one reference row per name
A name may belong to the top 100 in several decades. Put those results in separate columns so matching that name adds one reference row to each dog. Overall recognition means the name appears in any published record during the complete decades, 1880–2019.
```{r}
#| label: make-baby-name-reference
ssa_decades |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = decade, values_from = c(births, share, rank, top100),
    values_fill = list(births = 0, share = 0, top100 = FALSE)
  ) |>
  mutate(ssa_recognized = TRUE) |>
  arrange(name, .locale = "C") ->
  ssa_reference
```

## Inspect the top-100 cutoff
Compare the birth counts for the last name inside each top 100 and the first name outside it.

```{r}
#| label: inspect-the-top-100-cutoff
ssa_decades |>
  filter(rank %in% c(100L, 101L)) |>
  select(decade, rank, name, births) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = rank, values_from = c(name, births)) |>
  mutate(cutoff_tied = births_100 == births_101) ->
  ssa_cutoffs

ssa_cutoffs
```

## Save the baby-name tables
```{r}
#| label: save-baby-names
dir.create("data/derived", showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(ssa_reference, "data/derived/ssa_name_reference.csv", na = "")
write_csv(ssa_decades, "data/derived/ssa_name_decades.csv", na = "")
write_csv(ssa_cutoffs, "data/derived/ssa_top100_cutoffs.csv", na = "")
```

SSA omits names reported fewer than five times for a sex and year. Early birth years have less complete coverage because many people born before 1937 never applied for a Social Security card. These limits affect the historical comparisons.
